mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts before processing any later statements. This respects the chronological order of events in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Using a later statement that references X's count before updating X after the transfer, thus relying on an outdated value.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements that equate a signed difference to another difference as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side. This keeps the sign information intact.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence says "The number of items that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of items that A and B have" or any similar construction.
mathgap.example: Treating "X has more than Y" as an absolute difference |X‑Y| or swapping the order on the right‑hand side, losing the sign.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., "X has N items"), set that person's current count at that point in the narrative. Later statements may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence explicitly states a person's count.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is final after later transfers, ignoring subsequent updates that change the value.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives K items to Y", subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement is processed.
mathgap.example: Only adding K to Y without subtracting K from X, leaving the total number of items incorrect.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all statements into algebraic equations, collect them into a linear system and solve simultaneously for all unknowns, rather than handling equations in isolation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all statements have been parsed and before extracting the final answer.
mathgap.example: Solving each equation separately, which can produce inconsistent or incomplete values.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the linear system, before reporting the answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person's count is -3 or 4.5.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds should the transfer be performed.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement of the form "If X has more than N items, X will transfer ..." appears.
mathgap.example: Executing the transfer regardless of whether X's count exceeds the threshold.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount, pool their total and split it evenly, assigning the half to each person.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence mentions redistribution to equalize counts between two individuals.
mathgap.example: Giving each person half of the other's original count instead of half of the pooled total.

mathgap.title: Combined statements handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement contains multiple relational clauses (e.g., "X has N more than Y and M fewer than Z"), translate it into a set of equations that capture all relationships simultaneously.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence includes more than one comparison or sum.
mathgap.example: Treating each clause independently and ignoring the fact that they refer to the same variable, leading to contradictory constraints.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative scaling handling
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements of the form "The number of X increases by N times" as a multiplication: new count = old count × N (or × a fractional factor for non‑integer N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence mentions an increase by a factor, such as "increase by 2 times" or "increase by 5/3 times".
mathgap.example: Treating "increase by 2 times" as adding 2 to the count instead of doubling it.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets "X has more than Y" as |X‑Y|, discarding the sign and losing directionality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate such statements as signed differences preserving order: X ‑ Y = N.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model updates counts only after all statements are read, treating transfers as unordered operations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer immediately when it appears, before any later statements that may reference the updated counts.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as a permanent value, overlooking later transfers that modify it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current value at that point; allow subsequent statements to change them.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the transferred amount to the receiver but forgets to subtract it from the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Subtract the transferred amount from the giver as well as adding it to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model swaps the roles of X and Y, interpreting the statement as Y = X + N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "X has N more than Y" means X = Y + N (or X ‑ Y = N).

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats "difference between A and B" as an absolute difference, ignoring the order of A and B.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "difference between A and B" as the signed difference A ‑ B, preserving the given order.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by N times" as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads "increase by 2 times" as adding 2 (or adding twice the original) instead of scaling the count by a factor of 2.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "increase by N times" as a multiplicative scaling: new = old × N (or × fractional factor).
